title: Dependency Shadowboard & Cutover Ownership Protocol
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a lightweight, operational pattern called the 'Dependency Shadowboard' to capture, surface, and enforce ownership for dependencies that span engineering, design, infra, and security during roadmap cutovers. Many cross-team blockers today are discovered ad-hoc (Slack, hallway chats, or late PR reviews) and lead to missed cutovers or emergency rollbacks. This initiative defines the artifact, workflow, and escalation protocol to make hidden dependencies visible, assign explicit owners, and validate cutover readiness through a pre-flight checklist and simulated handoff exercises.
acceptance_criteria: A single searchable Confluence 'Shadowboard' page and API-backed index that lists active cross-team dependencies for the current cycle with owner, status, and cutover date.
Every roadmap ticket linked to at least one dependency entry or explicitly marked 'no external dependency' before merging to main release plan.
Automated reminders and escalation: owners receive a T-10 day and T-3 day reminder; unacknowledged items escalate to the team lead and PM.
Pilot: two initiatives (one infra-heavy, one feature-heavy) complete a simulated cutover using the shadowboard, and postmortem shows reduced last-minute infra/security tasks.
Metrics: time-to-acknowledge dependency assigned owner <= 48 hours during pilot; number of last-minute rollbacks due to untracked deps reduced by >= 50% in pilot teams.
milestones: Prototype Shadowboard schema + Confluence page + simple index (Feb 23 - Mar 5)
Automation: Slack/Email reminders + GitHub checklist template (Mar 8 - Mar 20)
Pilot with Platform & Mobile squads (Mar 22 - Apr 5)
Post-pilot retro and rollout plan (Apr 6 - Apr 15)
risks: Added process friction leads teams to mark dependencies as 'none' inaccurately.
Shadowboard becomes stale if ownership/TTL is not enforced.
Sensitive security dependencies may require redaction and cannot be fully public on Confluence — integration with the security ticketing flow will be needed.
Initial automation may create noisy reminders causing message fatigue.
notes: Design trade-off: embed shadowboard view into Console roadmap vs. keep in Confluence. Console integration offers better real-time visibility but increases implementation time and security surface.
We propose a minimal viable surface: a Confluence page + searchable index + Slack bot for T-10/T-3 reminders. Console integration scoped to follow-on release.

Ownership model: 'dependency owner' is a role on the dependency artifact (can be an individual or team). Cutover approver remains the ticket owner unless an explicit infra/security approver is required.
